131a-hurricane.png: Storm laboratory (Phase 21): a tropical cyclone — NHC definition and stages, Saffir-Simpson category from the wind (100 kt = Category 3), formation ingredients (Penn State and NASA disagree: 5° vs 8° from the equator), and Katrina from the NHC report (150 kt, 902 mb; 1392 deaths in the 2023 update).
131b-thunderstorm.png: Thunderstorm life cycle (NWS spotter guide): developing, mature, dissipating — at dissipation the downdraft overcomes the updraft; NSSL’s severe criteria as a check.
132a-sst.png: Earth weather atlas (Gate 21.2): January 2024 sea surface temperature (NOAA OISST v2.1, 1°), area-weighted global mean about 18.8 °C; the inspector reads the warm pool on the equator at 160° E; latitude profile on the right.
131c-winter.png: Winter storms: NSSL’s snow, sleet and freezing-rain profiles; NWS wind chill (10 °F, 40 mph) and the blizzard criteria (35 mph, ¼ mile, 3 hours).
132b-pressure-wind.png: July sea-level pressure (1991–2020 mean, NCEP/NCAR Reanalysis 1) with surface wind arrows: subtropical highs, the trade winds and the summer monsoon flow.
132c-globe.png: The same atlas on a 3D globe: July 2024 precipitation (GPCP v2.3, interim), the rain belt shifted north with the season.
133a-rainshadow.png: Regional climates (Gate 21.3): the rain shadow — Quillayute on the Olympic coast (2,574 mm a year, Cfb) against Yakima in the lee of the Cascades (204 mm, BSk), from NOAA 1991–2020 normals; Köppen–Geiger classes by Peel et al. (2007).
133b-mediterranean.png: Mediterranean summers: Los Angeles and San Francisco, wet winters and dry summers; by Peel’s criteria Los Angeles airport is just arid (BSk), a finding shown beside the National Park Service’s description.
134a-record.png: The global temperature record (Gate 21.4): NOAAGlobalTemp annual departures 1850–2025 from the 1901–2000 mean, with a 10-year running mean; 2024 is the warmest year at +1.26 °C.
